findings.before: When Inbox Classic starts, it shows the newest message of the first account’s Inbox, or of when you have several accounts.
findings.reason: All three platform startup callers now prefer a persisted folder/combined-view tree key. First Inbox/All Inboxes is only the fallback. Arrival chooses the remembered message row if present; grouped lists may select its conversation, so the final text must not promise displaying the exact saved child.
findings.proposed_and_final_correction: Inbox Classic reopens the folder or combined view you last used. It selects the last viewed message, or its conversation, if still listed. If there is no saved view to restore, it opens the first account’s Inbox, or when you have several accounts.
findings.target_scope: Exactly the startup paragraph of main-window.html in 28 non-English languages. Preserve ui-all-inboxes and markup; no outside-span changes.
findings.coordinated_finding: Grouped-conversation exception first raised by reading agent and confirmed by root; platform selected-row reader behavior also inspected here.

findings.reason: Mac/Linux mailto unsubscribe opened from a standalone message window still derives its compose account from the main mailbox. If the main window switched accounts, the draft can use that account. Windows explicitly uses the standalone message folder account. Related Linux app/mailbox files changed, but these caller bodies did not.
findings.existing_help_claim: Inbox Classic prepares the requested email from the account you are reading the message in, with that account’s signature.
findings.proposed_scope: No new round5 target edit proposed because this is the previously documented runtime inconsistency and unchanged caller chain. Root may retain the prior disclosure or fix the account propagation in a separate code task.
findings.validation: Static caller comparison only, no GUI reproduction.

retained_decisions.reason: Preserving Message-ID multiplicity and newest matching N copies fixes implementation of existing many-message Undo promises. No new restriction requiring help wording. Refused-move rows now win over successor-row selection.

Connection failures leave flag/read intent pending for retry before next folder sync. Explicit server refusal clears/reverses it and uses existing localized undone messages. Help already says server changes happen in background and other apps see them after success/sync; no inspected claim promises immediate server success or rollback on connection loss.

New menu placements reuse localized command identities for Tools > Message Rules/Encryption Keys and Message > Create Rule from Message, matching existing help paths. Assertions are developer diagnostics, not missing localized product labels.

Visible-page loading, blank-row refill, preserving the clicked message during asynchronous reload, scroll retention and exactly-once draft opening support existing UI selection/action claims. No new user-facing hardcoded string found in inspected production changes. Test-only observation/report strings are excluded.
IMAP operations now use chunks of up to 1,000 UIDs; this is an internal command batch size, not a new limit on UI selection. The distinct agent 1,000-eligible-message limit has not changed.

Adjacent brand/logo and sign-in-code wording speaks generally of provider-confirmed domains/signatures and does not promise Authentication-Results as the only carrier. Detailed ARC trust logic and connections paragraph are owned by the other agent.
Deep-test drivers, synchronization observation, JSON notes and missing-driver error are test/tooling surfaces. Do not infer shipped user labels from these diagnostic strings.
